Ivy is a song about a widow that misses her late husband terribly, & is trying to enter a new relationship despite that. Spoiler alert: it isn’t working. Thread below!

This is the line that confirms she’s a widow, essentially saying “the old widow does this BUT I, the young widow, do this.” She’s grieving for the living because they are living without her late husband.

This is interesting — never once does the widow say that she and her lover are physically doing anything together. These are just images & feelings, which supports the theory that the person she loves is dead. She’s going into nature to talk to and be with his spirit.
Stole is past tense, not present. The moments that they’ve stolen have already passed, ie. the untimely death of her husband. Their whole relationship was on borrowed time.
